intro: One medium orange is roughly 60 kcal (estimate). Almost all the calories come from natural sugar, along with fibre and vitamin C.
diet: Definitely. Oranges are a fresh, low-calorie snack that keeps you full. The one to watch is orange juice, because one glass uses 2-3 oranges without the fibre. Eating the whole fruit fills you up more than drinking juice. One or two a day is totally okay.
tips: Eat the whole orange, not juice, so you keep the fibre.
Keep oranges on your office desk for a tea-time snack.
During Chinese New Year, keep count of the mandarin oranges. Very easy to overeat.

swap.name: Fresh orange instead of boxed orange juice
swap.why: Half the calories, has fibre, no added sugar.

faq.a: Oranges are high in vitamin C, which supports the immune system, but they're not a cure for colds.

faq.q: Is it okay to eat oranges on an empty stomach?
faq.a: For most people, okay. If you have gastric issues, some people feel discomfort, so eat it after other food.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the white part of the orange?
faq.a: No need. The white part has fibre, you can eat it together.
